The user wants an educational visualization of nuclear fusion—likely showing atomic nuclei colliding, overcoming electrostatic repulsion, and releasing energy as they fuse into heavier elements like helium.

I'll build this in five steps: initialize the scene with post-processing bloom, create deuterium and tritium spheres with proton/neutron textures, animate them accelerating toward each other under heat/pressure, trigger the fusion event with a particle burst representing the neutron and helium release, and add UI overlays explaining each phase of the process.

I'm writing code for SphereGeometry instances representing hydrogen isotopes, a Points particle system for the energy burst and background plasma, animated positions using lerp for the collision trajectory, PointLights with intensity spikes for the flash, and post-processing bloom to simulate the intense heat glow during fusion.
Spinning up the sandbox environment now to render the fusion sequence with camera orbits and real-time lighting updates.

I've created an interactive 3D visualization showing deuterium and tritium nuclei accelerating under extreme heat, fusing into helium with a bright energy burst and neutron release, complete with glowing plasma effects to illustrate how stars and fusion reactors generate power.
